$comment: SEED SET for the CALIBRATION.md §3 case-law coding protocol. NOT YET CODED.
These are the five decisions the paper already relies on. Every `factors` value is
null and every `quotes` entry is empty: that is the point. Filling them in requires
reading each decision and is the one task that cannot be done from inside this
repository. Nulls are deliberate rather than defaulted to zero, so that an uncoded
case can never be silently fitted as if it scored zero on everything.
Protocol reminders that the harness enforces (see calibration/coding.ts):
- Expand this set by citator to N ≈ 15–30 (§3.1).
- TWO independent coders, blind to each other and to the hypothesis (§3.3).
- Per-factor Cohen's κ. κ < 0.6 on any factor means rewrite the rubric and recode
that factor — it does not mean proceed with a caveat.
- A supporting quotation per coded factor. A code without a quote is not auditable.
precommit            0 = post-hoc engagement · 1 = protocol/retainer predating the incident
separation           0 none · 1 partial · 2 demonstrably separate workstream
significant_purpose  0 purely business · 1 mixed · 2 legal advice a significant purpose
valve                0 conclusions circulated widely · 1 limited · 2 tightly held
notes: Uncoded seed. supportedTier will remain T4 until this is completed and κ reported.

codings.citation: In re Target Corp. Customer Data Sec. Breach Litig., 2015 WL 6777384 (D. Minn. Oct. 23, 2015)
codings.expectedDirection: Protection SURVIVED. The paper reads this as turning on a two-track structure set up in advance. Confirm against the opinion rather than assuming.

codings.citation: In re Capital One Consumer Data Sec. Breach Litig., 2020 WL 2731238 (E.D. Va. May 26, 2020)
codings.expectedDirection: Protection FAILED. Widely read as the would-have-been-done-anyway case: the same vendor under a pre-existing SOW.

codings.citation: In re Rutter's Inc. Data Sec. Breach Litig., 2021 WL 3733137 (M.D. Pa. July 22, 2021)
Guo Wengui v. Clark Hill, PLC, 338 F.R.D. 7 (D.D.C. 2021)
codings.expectedDirection: Protection FAILED. Two-track approach rejected on these facts — worth coding carefully, since the paper's architecture is a two-track design and this is the case against it.

codings.citation: In re Kellogg Brown & Root, Inc., 756 F.3d 754 (D.C. Cir. 2014)
codings.expectedDirection: Protection UPHELD. Source of the significant-purpose test. Not a breach-forensics case — record that in notes, since it stretches the sample frame in §3.1.
